info.title: ltx/ltx-video-to-video-hdr
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "ltx/ltx-video-to-video-hdr", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. `x-comfy-router-input-modalities` records the media kinds the model is documented to accept; the request schema is shared across sibling models and may admit media kinds this model ignores. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

post.summary: Queued-only: this route answers 403 not_enabled for ltx/ltx-video-to-video-hdr; use POST /v2/models/ltx/ltx-video-to-video-hdr/requests.

schema.description: Request body for `POST /proxy/ltx/v2/video-to-video-hdr`. On Comfy Router this model runs on the queued route only (`POST /v2/models/ltx/ltx-video-to-video-hdr/requests`): a job can outlast the time a synchronous call is held, so the synchronous route refuses it.

output_colorspace.description: Color space of the OpenEXR frame sequence at `result.exr_frames_url`. It does not affect `result.video_url`.

video_uri.description: Input video as a publicly accessible HTTPS URL or a base64 data URI. H.264 or HEVC in MP4, MOV or MKV, up to 200 MB by URL. Width and height must fit within 3840x2160 in either orientation.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for LTX SDR to HDR: the terminal `LTXVideoToVideoHDRJobStatusResponse` poll document, forwarded unchanged. The job is submit-and-poll and Router polls on the caller's behalf, so the body a caller receives is the finished job (`status: completed`) rather than the task handle the underlying submit returns.
`result.video_url` is the HDR video and `result.exr_frames_url` is a ZIP of per-frame OpenEXR images in the requested `output_colorspace`. `result` is only present on a completed job. Output URLs expire 24 hours after completion, so download promptly rather than storing the link. A failed job carries `error.type` and `error.message` instead of `result`.

result.description: Present when status is completed; output URLs expire 24 hours after completion

exr_frames_url.description: URL of a ZIP of per-frame OpenEXR images in the requested color space

video_url.description: URL of the HDR video, a 10-bit HEVC BT.2020/HLG MP4
